description: Shared Renovate configuration for coo-quack repositories.

packageRules.description: Stable releases only. ignoreUnstable stops protecting a package once its current version is itself unstable: Renovate then follows the prerelease channel, so a repo that adopted an alpha (sensitive-canary's vitepress 2.0.0-alpha) keeps receiving alphas. Excluding hyphenated versions leaves exactly the stable channel, because an npm version containing a hyphen is always a prerelease. Scoped to the npm datasource; in other ecosystems a hyphen appears in stable versions too (Docker tags like 1.2-alpine), so the same regex would block legitimate updates there.

Never pin a constraint. engines, peerDependencies and required_version state the range a package supports, not a version it depends on. Rewriting one to an exact version narrows what can install the package, and in a published manifest it forces that version on every consumer.

No major bumps for override targets. An override exists to lift a transitive package out of an advisory window while staying inside what its parent declared; a major takes it outside that, substituting a version the parent never asked for. Renovate raised talkative-lobster's fast-uri override from 3.1.4 to 4.1.1 and automerged it, while ajv declared ^3.0.1 and its newest release still does. When only a major would fix something, the parent needs upgrading, and that is a decision rather than a bump.
Automerge everything once CI passes. Required checks are the gate; a release that breaks a repo turns them red and the merge stops there.
Keep the package manager itself current, wherever a repo pins one through packageManager.
One PR for devDependencies rather than one each.
